jurisdiction: United States research pilot; creator terms, learner agreements, platform rules and applicable federal/state privacy, accessibility and advertising requirements require authorized review.
source_frame: Action Model system-map industry slug course_creators; taxonomy reference only, not client demand or implementation proof.
scope_note: Research covers content production, course administration, learner support and claims/accessibility review for independently operated online courses. No learner records, creator accounts, payment credentials or live course changes were accessed.
summary: Independent creators can test supervised assistance for organizing course content, handling routine learner-support triage and reconciling course administration. Accessibility checks, learner privacy, rights, refunds, factual claims and final publication/support authority remain human gates; vendor feature pages and open-source repositories establish capabilities, not adoption or savings.

automation_research.finding: W3C WCAG 2.2 provides accessibility success criteria, while U.S. Department of Education FERPA guidance describes rights and obligations for covered education records and NIST frames privacy as a risk-management activity. These sources support bounded checklists and evidence capture, not autonomous compliance, instructional or business decisions.
automation_research.forecast_note: No independent course-creator automation rate, adoption prevalence or measured savings was found; product and repository capability is not realized automation or outcome evidence.

software.name: Teachable
software.capability: Vendor presents hosted tools for creating and selling online courses, including course content, learner access and creator administration.
software.price_note: Pricing, transaction costs, plan limits, migration effort and avoidable spend are client-specific and unmeasured.

software.capability: Vendor presents an online-business platform combining course/content delivery with creator marketing, customer and administration features.

modules.capability: Shared inbox and customer-support conversation management documented by the upstream product and repository.
modules.reuse_shape: Learner-support inbox triage, tagging and draft replies with explicit human send authority; do not make it the learner-record authority.
modules.rights_state: Upstream repository and product licensing/edition terms require review before any hosted or forked reuse; preserve source notices and external-channel credentials.
modules.limits: Documentation does not prove learner identity mapping, privacy isolation, response quality, consent, retention or support outcomes.

modules.capability: Data platform and API/admin interface suitable as a controlled content and course-operations record layer, as described by the upstream repository.
modules.reuse_shape: Model course versions, lesson metadata, review status and support queue references behind SISO identity/ACL; keep payment and learner authority boundaries explicit.
modules.rights_state: Upstream license, edition boundaries and deployment obligations require independent review; repository capability is not production qualification.
modules.limits: A configurable data layer does not prove tenant isolation, FERPA applicability, retention/deletion correctness, export/restore or instructional record authority.

modules.capability: Workflow automation with reusable connectors, triggers and actions documented by the upstream repository.
modules.reuse_shape: Allowlisted notifications, checklist creation and support-routing workflows; require approval for learner-facing sends, refunds, access changes or publication.
modules.rights_state: Repository distinguishes community code and commercially licensed/enterprise paths; edition, hosting, connector terms and rights require review.
modules.limits: Connectors do not prove idempotency, privacy controls, reliable retries, learner consent, account authorization or acceptable support outcomes.

processes.process: Course outline, lesson assets and accessibility-ready publishing preparation
processes.automation_boundary: Organize supplied lesson material, generate a draft checklist and flag missing headings, captions, alternatives or contrast evidence; do not invent instructional claims, copy, rights or accessibility conformance.
processes.baseline_required: Matched lessons, creator and reviewer minutes including rework, accessibility defects found after review, publication delay and actual tool/operator cost.
processes.metric: Human minutes per accepted lesson, including review and rework; unresolved WCAG-related issues, rights exceptions and factual corrections.
processes.falsifier: Reject if review/rework does not reduce net effort or a critical accessibility, rights, privacy or instructional-quality defect reaches publication.
processes.human_authority: Creator or named instructional/accessibility reviewer owns lesson content, claims, rights and final publication decision; WCAG is a reference standard, not an automated approval.

processes.process: Course versioning, learner access administration and routine enrollment operations
processes.automation_boundary: Record approved course/version metadata, route routine access requests and surface exceptions; do not independently grant/ revoke access, issue refunds or alter payment/entitlement authority.
processes.baseline_required: Matched enrollment/access cases, handling and review minutes, rework and exception counts, access-error rate, refund/escalation latency and actual spend.
processes.metric: Human minutes per correctly resolved administration case, including review and exceptions; unauthorized access, missed revocation and entitlement errors.
processes.falsifier: Reject if exception/review effort offsets time reduction or any unauthorized access, mistaken revocation, refund error or unlogged authority transition occurs.
processes.human_authority: Creator or authorized platform/payment operator owns entitlement, refund, account and access decisions; automation may route and record only.

processes.process: Learner question intake, triage and response drafting
processes.automation_boundary: Classify and route routine questions, retrieve approved course facts and draft replies; do not provide individualized professional advice, disclose another learner's data or send without human review.
processes.baseline_required: Matched support cases, first-response and resolution minutes including review/rework, escalation rate, privacy incidents, incorrect-answer rate and support tooling cost.
processes.metric: Human minutes per accepted response, including triage, review and escalations; incorrect, privacy-sensitive or unresolved responses.
processes.falsifier: Reject if net handling effort is not reduced or a privacy leak, unsafe/incorrect guidance, missed escalation or unapproved external send occurs.
processes.human_authority: Named support operator owns response, escalation and any refund/access decision; specialist or professional questions remain with the appropriate qualified human.

processes.process: Course claims, testimonials and learner-feedback review
processes.automation_boundary: Collect source links, organize feedback and flag unsupported or inconsistent claims for review; do not decide truth, endorsement disclosure, outcome guarantees or whether a course is suitable.
processes.baseline_required: Matched claims/feedback items, sourcing and reviewer minutes including rework, correction/removal rate, unresolved evidence exceptions and tooling cost.
processes.metric: Human minutes per approved claim or feedback item, including provenance review and rework; unsupported, misleading, privacy-sensitive or unresolvable items.
processes.falsifier: Reject if review/rework does not reduce net effort or an unsupported outcome, fabricated testimonial, privacy violation or missing provenance survives approval.
processes.human_authority: Creator and authorized legal/advertising reviewer own claims, disclosures, consent, redaction and publication decisions; automation cannot make professional or regulatory determinations.

pilot.design: Small matched pilot of approved lessons, administration cases, support cases and claims/feedback items; log automation time, human review/rework, exceptions, privacy/accessibility/claims defects, escalations and final authority decisions.
record: automation, review, rework and exception minutes
reject_if: net human effort does not fall after review and exception work
critical quality, accessibility, privacy, rights or authority condition fails
results cannot be reproduced with source records and human decisions

limitations: No independent adoption, market-size, conversion, completion, retention or savings evidence was used.
Vendor pages and repositories describe capabilities only; no account, deployment, learner data or outcome was tested.
Accessibility, privacy, advertising/claims and consumer-protection applicability varies by course, audience, state and platform and needs authorized review.
FERPA may not apply to an independent creator; its inclusion is a scope check, not a legal conclusion.
No payment, refund, credentialing, assessment or professional-advice workflow is admitted to automation.
